evals.prompt: Run idd start for: Add trainer RUT, birth date, bank data, and include trainers in exports without bank data. The repository has stable Git state and native interactive questioning.
evals.expected_output: IDD creates a managed workflow, routes the change, enters the appropriate grilling mode automatically, uses structured questions for product decisions, and after confirmation auto-writes the spec instead of making the user copy a spec command.
expectations: A managed workflow JSON is created in the Git common metadata directory.
The workflow records a destination and domain/size classification.
Interactive structured questioning is used when available.
No subagents are used for grilling or spec.
After shared understanding, spec is generated in the same session without requiring a manual phase command.
The session stops at the fresh implementation boundary and tells the user to run idd continue.

evals.prompt: Run idd continue. The only active managed NORMAL workflow has a READY spec, a planning checkpoint, and next action IMPLEMENT. The worktree is clean.
evals.expected_output: IDD resolves the workflow without asking for a spec path, implements it, verifies it, creates one local candidate checkpoint, persists base/candidate SHAs, and stops for independent review.
expectations: The active workflow is resolved from Git metadata without user reconstruction.
The implementation uses the exact active spec stored in workflow state.
A stable local candidate commit is created only after required verification.
Unrelated changes are not staged or committed.
Workflow state records exact base and candidate SHAs and REVIEW_REQUIRED.
The only recommended fresh-session command is idd continue.

evals.prompt: Run idd continue in a fresh reviewer session. The active workflow says REVIEW_REQUIRED with base abc111 and candidate def222 for docs/specs/trainer-data.md.
evals.expected_output: IDD performs an INITIAL independent review of exactly abc111..def222 rather than reviewing arbitrary branch state.
expectations: The review range is exact base..candidate from workflow state.
The review covers spec fidelity and engineering quality.
No code/spec files are modified.
APPROVE marks the workflow DONE; CHANGES REQUIRED writes a ledger and routes the same unit to corrective implementation.
The next fresh-session command is idd continue when work remains.

evals.prompt: A LARGE workflow has children 03 and 04. A proposed candidate commit for child 03 contains implementation files clearly belonging to both children. Run idd review for child 03.
evals.expected_output: IDD refuses to treat the mixed commit as an isolated child candidate and does not recommend separate duplicate reviews of the same giant diff.
expectations: Candidate isolation failure is detected.
The reviewer does not APPROVE or run a fake independent child review over the mixed candidate.
The response reports recovery/replan guidance rather than reviewing child 03 and child 04 independently against the same diff.
No sibling is marked DONE without its own isolated APPROVE lineage.

evals.prompt: Run idd continue for a LARGE workflow. Children 01-04 are DONE, child 05 is READY with all dependencies DONE, child 06 is blocked by 05, and no claims exist.
evals.expected_output: IDD computes frontier=[05] and proceeds deterministically to child 05 implementation without asking the user which child comes next.
expectations: Frontier is computed from dependencies and state rather than a stale README next-step line.
Child 05 is claimed before implementation.
Child 06 is not selected while blocked.
The user is not asked a ceremonial choice when there is exactly one frontier child.

evals.prompt: Run idd continue for a LARGE workflow with two READY independent frontier children. The user previously enabled subagents for implementation and the host supports isolated worktrees.
evals.expected_output: IDD may claim both children and dispatch isolated implementations in separate worktrees/branches, keeping one candidate lineage per child.
expectations: Delegation preference is read from persisted workflow state.
Each child gets an explicit claim and base SHA.
Concurrent child edits do not share an overlapping working tree.
Each child produces its own candidate commit and later review lineage.
The primary agent owns integration and workflow state.

evals.prompt: Run idd continue after a child APPROVE. Workflow fog contains 'final onboarding integration after CLI contract is stable'. The approved child now makes that outcome precise without requiring a new product decision.
evals.expected_output: IDD reevaluates fog and graduates the newly sharp in-scope outcome into a child instead of prematurely declaring the workflow complete.
expectations: Fog is reevaluated after child approval.
A newly precise required outcome becomes a child with dependencies.
No user question is asked when the child boundary is deterministic from approved contracts and repository facts.
Parent review is not recommended until the new required child is DONE.

evals.prompt: Run idd continue after an INITIAL review returned CHANGES REQUIRED for candidate def222. The ledger has B1 and I1 open. A fresh implementation session is starting.
evals.expected_output: IDD automatically enters corrective implementation for the same unit, fixes only B1/I1 and affected seams, creates a corrective candidate commit, and stops for corrective review.
expectations: No spec path or finding text needs to be pasted by the user.
The open ledger is read before broad exploration.
Corrective implementation is scoped to material open findings.
The corrective candidate lineage records previous candidate and new SHA.
The next command at the isolation boundary is idd continue.

evals.prompt: Run idd status. The child spec README says child 03 and 04 are next, but workflow state says 03 DONE, 04 DONE, 05 READY; Git candidate/review evidence agrees with workflow state.
evals.expected_output: IDD reports workflow state as authoritative, identifies the README progress prose as stale non-authoritative duplication, and shows child 05 as next deterministic action.
expectations: Dynamic execution truth comes from reconciled workflow/Git evidence, not README prose.
No approved child is reopened merely because README is stale.
Status displays destination, frontier, candidates, and next action clearly.

evals.prompt: Run idd start for a NORMAL feature. Grilling is complete, the spec is READY, and the user has not said whether to implement now or create issues. Native structured questioning is available.
evals.expected_output: IDD asks exactly one two-option delivery question: EXECUTE or ISSUES, with no third formal disposition.
expectations: The delivery question appears only after executable READY work exists.
Exactly two choices are offered: execute now or take it to issues.
No spec-only/later/park third option is invented.
The selected disposition is persisted in workflow state and is not asked again.

evals.prompt: Run idd start for a NORMAL READY feature where the user already said: 'Llévalo a issues, no implementes'. A writable GitHub Issues integration is available.
evals.expected_output: IDD skips the delivery question, creates the planning checkpoint, publishes one thin issue pointing to the spec, marks the workflow PLANNED, and does not implement code.
expectations: Natural-language ISSUES intent is recognized without asking again.
A stable planning checkpoint exists before issue publication.
Exactly one implementation issue is created for the NORMAL spec.
The issue points to the spec and does not copy the entire spec body.
Workflow state stores tracker/issue ref and status PLANNED.
No implementation is started.

evals.prompt: A LARGE workflow has a READY parent spec, three sharp child specs, one fog item, and delivery disposition ISSUES. Publish the plan to a tracker with native parent/child and dependency support.
evals.expected_output: IDD creates one parent/index issue plus one issue per sharp child, wires dependencies, leaves fog un-ticketed, and parks the workflow.
expectations: The parent issue acts as an index rather than duplicating the parent spec.
Each sharp child spec gets exactly one thin issue.
Native parent-child and dependency relationships are used when available.
Fog does not become an issue prematurely.
Workflow status becomes PLANNED and no child implementation begins.

evals.prompt: Run idd continue on a PLANNED ISSUES workflow with no active issue. Two child issues are currently executable.
evals.expected_output: IDD does not choose or implement either backlog issue. It reports the parked state and tells the user to start an issue explicitly.
expectations: continue does not claim or implement a backlog issue.
The executable issue refs are surfaced for the user.
The next action uses idd start <issue ref/url>, not idd continue to start backlog work.
Workflow remains PLANNED.

evals.prompt: Run idd start #123. Issue #123 was created by IDD for child 03 and contains workflow/spec markers. Its dependencies are DONE and its workflow is PLANNED.
evals.expected_output: IDD resolves the existing workflow and child spec, claims the issue, begins delivery without asking EXECUTE vs ISSUES again, and uses continue only at later isolation boundaries.
expectations: The issue marker resolves the exact workflow and spec.
Dependencies are checked before implementation.
The issue is claimed/assigned when tracker capability and identity allow it.
No delivery-disposition question is asked because starting the issue explicitly means execute it.
The same issue remains active through corrective review loops.
On APPROVE the issue is completed/closed when permitted and the LARGE workflow returns to PLANNED rather than auto-starting another issue.
